title: Creamy Stovetop Butter Chicken with Garlic Naan
dek: Yogurt-spiced chicken thighs simmer in a silky tomato, butter and cream sauce, then meet warm garlic naan for a richly flavored Indian-inspired dinner.
image_alt: Orange butter chicken curry with visible chicken pieces and cilantro beside a stack of charred garlic naan
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs, trimmed and cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
4 garlic cloves, finely grated and divided
4 tsp finely grated fresh ginger, divided
1/4 cup cilantro leaves and tender stems, roughly chopped

instructions.name: Marinate the chicken
instructions.text: Combine the chicken, yogurt, lemon juice, half the garlic, half the ginger, 1 teaspoon garam masala, 1 teaspoon cumin, 1 teaspoon paprika, the turmeric and 3/4 teaspoon salt. Coat every piece, cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes or up to 8 hours. Do not leave the raw chicken at room temperature.

instructions.name: Heat the broiler
instructions.text: Position a rack 6 inches below the broiler and heat the broiler to high. Line a heavy rimmed sheet pan with foil, set an oven-safe wire rack over it and lightly oil the rack. Arrange the chicken in one uncrowded layer, letting excess marinade drip back into the bowl.

instructions.name: Broil the chicken safely
instructions.text: Broil for 6 minutes, turn the pieces and broil for 4 to 6 minutes more, until lightly charred and the thickest pieces reach 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Transfer to a clean plate. Discard the raw marinade and wash anything that touched it.

instructions.name: Soften the onion
instructions.text: While the chicken broils, heat the oil and 1 tablespoon butter in a wide Dutch oven or deep 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until very soft and golden at the edges.

instructions.name: Bloom the aromatics
instructions.text: Add the remaining garlic and ginger and cook for 45 seconds. Stir in the remaining 2 teaspoons garam masala, 1 teaspoon cumin, 1 teaspoon paprika and the cayenne, if using. Cook for 30 seconds, just until fragrant, then stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute.

instructions.name: Reduce the tomato base
instructions.text: Add the crushed tomatoes and water, scraping up the browned seasoning. Bring to a lively simmer, then reduce the heat to medium-low and cook uncovered for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick enough to leave a brief trail behind a spoon.

instructions.name: Make the sauce silky
instructions.text: For an especially smooth sauce, blend the tomato mixture directly in the pot with an immersion blender, keeping the blade submerged. Stir in the cream, brown sugar and remaining 2 tablespoons butter over low heat. Simmer gently for 2 minutes; do not boil hard after adding the cream.

instructions.name: Finish the butter chicken
instructions.text: Fold the cooked chicken and any clean plate juices into the sauce. Simmer gently for 3 to 4 minutes, until the sauce coats the pieces and the chicken is hot throughout. Taste and add a small pinch of salt only if needed.

instructions.name: Warm the naan and serve
instructions.text: Wrap the naan in foil and warm in a 350°F oven for 5 to 7 minutes, or heat each piece briefly in a dry skillet. Spoon the vivid orange butter chicken into shallow bowls, scatter with cilantro and serve one warm naan alongside each portion, matching the photographed presentation.

why_it_works: A short yogurt marinade seasons the chicken throughout and encourages browning while thighs stay juicy under the intense broiler heat.
Cooking the tomato base until concentrated removes raw acidity before cream and butter soften it into a glossy, balanced sauce.
Broiling the chicken separately produces charred edges without overcrowding the sauce pot, then a brief final simmer reunites the flavors without overcooking the meat.
swaps: Use 1 1/2 pounds boneless skinless chicken breast cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces; begin checking at 8 total broiling minutes and still cook to 165°F.
For a lighter sauce, replace the heavy cream with full-fat canned coconut milk; the flavor will be less traditional but the sauce remains stable and creamy.
Plain naan or roti can replace garlic naan. For a gluten-free meal, serve with certified gluten-free flatbread or steamed basmati rice.
storage: Cool the butter chicken promptly and refrigerate it in a shallow airtight container within 2 hours for up to 4 days; keep naan separate for up to 2 days. Reheat the curry gently on the stovetop with a splash of water, stirring often, until it reaches 165°F. Warm naan in a 350°F oven for 4 to 5 minutes. Freeze the curry, without naan, for up to 2 months and thaw overnight in the refrigerator.
notes: Whole-milk Greek yogurt clings to the chicken better than thin yogurt; shake off only the loose excess so the coating can char instead of drip and burn.
Garam masala brands vary in intensity. Use the measured amount first, then add no more than 1/4 teaspoon at the end if a stronger aroma is wanted.
Keep the cream sauce at a gentle simmer. Vigorous boiling can split the dairy and make the finished curry look oily instead of smooth.

faqs.q: Can I cook the marinated chicken in a skillet instead of broiling it?
faqs.a: Yes. Shake off excess marinade and sear the chicken in two batches in a lightly oiled 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat for 7 to 9 minutes total, turning until browned and 165°F. Crowding the pan will steam the coating, so keep the batches separate.

faqs.q: Why does my butter chicken sauce taste sharply acidic?
faqs.a: The crushed tomatoes probably need more reduction. Simmer the tomato base uncovered until thick before adding dairy, then use the measured brown sugar rather than adding extra cream. Salt also rounds out acidity, so adjust it only after the chicken returns to the sauce.

faqs.q: Can I prepare butter chicken ahead for a dinner party?
faqs.a: Yes. Make the complete curry up to 2 days ahead, cool it quickly and refrigerate. Reheat slowly to 165°F, loosening with a tablespoon or two of water, and add the cilantro only at serving time. Warm the naan just before eating.

title: Deep-Dish Spinach & Feta Lattice Pie with Dill
dek: Golden puff-pastry lattice encloses a generous, sliceable filling of dry spinach, tangy feta, ricotta and fresh dill in this substantial Greek-inspired bake.
image_alt: Thick slices of golden lattice pie filled with dark green spinach, white feta and herbs on parchment
ingredients: 2 packages frozen chopped spinach, 16 oz each, thawed
4 scallions, white and green parts thinly sliced
12 oz block feta, crumbled into 1/2-inch pieces
8 oz whole-milk ricotta, drained if watery
1 package frozen all-butter puff pastry, 17.3 oz with 2 sheets, thawed in the refrigerator
1 large egg beaten with 1 tbsp water, for egg wash

instructions.name: Dry the spinach thoroughly
instructions.text: Place the thawed spinach in a clean lint-free towel in four batches and twist firmly over the sink until no more liquid drips out. Break apart the compacted spinach with your fingers. You should have about 4 tightly packed cups; excess water would make the deep filling gummy.

instructions.name: Cook the aromatics
instructions.text: Heat the olive oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/2 teaspoon salt and cook for 7 to 8 minutes, until soft and translucent. Add the scallions and garlic and cook for 1 minute. Spread the mixture on a plate and cool for 10 minutes.

instructions.name: Mix the filling
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the dry spinach, cooled onion mixture, black pepper, nutmeg, feta, ricotta, eggs, dill, parsley, lemon zest and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt. Fold just until evenly mixed, leaving visible pieces of feta like those in the finished slices.

instructions.name: Prepare the pan and pastry
instructions.text: Heat the oven to 400°F with a heavy sheet pan on the center rack. Line a deep 9-inch square metal baking pan with a parchment sling. On a lightly floured surface, roll one cold puff-pastry sheet to a 12-inch square and fit it across the bottom and up the sides. Refrigerate the lined pan.

instructions.name: Cut the lattice strips
instructions.text: Roll the second cold pastry sheet to a 10-inch square. Cut it into eight even 1 1/4-inch strips with a sharp knife or pizza wheel. Set the strips on parchment and refrigerate them while filling the pie; cold pastry holds a cleaner lattice and rises higher.

instructions.name: Add the deep spinach layer
instructions.text: Spread the filling evenly inside the cold pastry shell and press it gently into the corners without compacting it hard. Trim the pastry walls to a 1-inch overhang. The filling should remain visibly thick and green, with distinct white feta pockets throughout.

instructions.name: Weave and glaze the lattice
instructions.text: Arrange four pastry strips parallel across the filling. Fold back alternating strips, add one crosswise strip and unfold; repeat with the remaining strips to form a loose lattice. Trim the ends, fold the bottom-crust overhang inward and press to seal. Brush exposed pastry with egg wash and add sesame seeds if using.

instructions.name: Bake until deeply golden
instructions.text: Set the pie pan directly on the preheated sheet pan and bake for 48 to 55 minutes, rotating once, until the lattice and side crust are deep golden and the center of the egg-bound filling reaches 165°F. If the lattice browns before the center is hot, tent loosely with foil.

instructions.name: Rest and cut cleanly
instructions.text: Cool in the pan for 20 minutes so the filling sets and steam escapes from the crust. Use the parchment sling to lift the pie, then cut into 8 rectangles with a serrated knife. Each piece should show a golden lattice, dark spinach and white feta pockets, matching the photograph.

why_it_works: Aggressively squeezing the thawed spinach removes enough water for a tall filling that slices cleanly without soaking the puff pastry.
Cooling the cooked aromatics protects the eggs from scrambling, while feta pieces and drained ricotta create both tangy pockets and a cohesive interior.
Cold pastry and a preheated sheet pan encourage a crisp base and defined lattice, while a 20-minute rest lets the deep filling stabilize before cutting.
swaps: Use 3 pounds fresh mature spinach instead of frozen: wilt it in batches, cool completely, chop and squeeze until very dry before measuring 4 packed cups.
Replace ricotta with 8 ounces well-drained full-fat cottage cheese pulsed briefly until mostly smooth; do not substitute additional salty feta one-for-one.
Frozen pie dough can replace puff pastry for a denser, less flaky crust; roll both rounds into squares, make the same lattice and bake until the filling reaches 165°F.
storage: Refrigerate cooled spinach pie in an airtight container within 2 hours for up to 4 days. Reheat uncovered on a rack over a sheet pan at 350°F for 15 to 20 minutes, until crisp and 165°F in the center; microwaving softens the pastry. Freeze baked slices for up to 2 months, thaw overnight in the refrigerator and reheat the same way.
notes: Keep puff pastry cold but flexible. If it becomes soft or greasy while rolling or weaving, refrigerate it on parchment for 10 minutes before continuing.
Block feta holds recognizable white pockets better than precrumbled feta, which is often dry and coated to prevent clumping.
A light-colored metal pan on a preheated sheet pan browns the bottom more reliably than glass. If using glass, do not place it on preheated metal because thermal shock can break it.

faqs.q: Why is my spinach-and-feta pie filling watery?
faqs.a: The spinach or ricotta retained too much liquid, or the pie was cut while piping hot. Squeeze the spinach in small batches until completely dry, drain loose ricotta and rest the baked pie for the full 20 minutes before slicing.

faqs.q: Can I assemble the spinach pie a day ahead?
faqs.a: Yes. Assemble and glaze it, cover the pan tightly and refrigerate for up to 18 hours. Add a fresh light coat of egg wash before baking directly from the refrigerator, allowing 5 to 10 extra minutes and verifying a 165°F center.

faqs.q: How do I keep the puff-pastry lattice defined?
faqs.a: Thaw the pastry only until flexible, roll on a lightly floured surface and chill the cut strips before weaving. Do not stretch the lattice tight, and brush only the exposed top with egg wash so the cut edges can expand freely.

title: Warm Sticky Toffee Pudding with Pecan Toffee Sauce
dek: Soft individual date puddings are unmolded beneath a glossy brown-sugar toffee sauce and toasted pecans for a make-ahead British-inspired dessert.
image_alt: Individual sticky toffee pudding covered in thick golden toffee sauce and topped with chopped toasted pecans
ingredients: 8 oz pitted Medjool dates, finely chopped
6 tbsp unsalted butter, softened, plus more for the ramekins
1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, spooned and leveled
1/2 cup pecan halves, toasted and roughly chopped
6 tbsp unsalted butter, cut into pieces, for the sauce
3/4 cup packed dark brown sugar, for the sauce
1 tsp pure vanilla extract, for the sauce
1/4 tsp kosher salt, for the sauce

instructions.name: Soften the dates
instructions.text: Put the chopped dates in a heatproof bowl, pour over the boiling water and stir in the baking soda. Let stand for 15 minutes, until the dates are very soft and the liquid looks foamy. Mash with a fork, leaving a few small pieces for texture.

instructions.name: Prepare the ramekins
instructions.text: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the center. Generously butter eight 6-ounce oven-safe ramekins, place a parchment circle in the bottom of each and arrange them on a rimmed sheet pan. The parchment makes the warm puddings release cleanly.

instructions.name: Cream the butter and sugar
instructions.text: Beat the softened butter and 3/4 cup brown sugar in a large bowl with an electric mixer on medium speed for 2 to 3 minutes, until lighter and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, scraping the bowl after each, then mix in 1 teaspoon vanilla.

instructions.name: Combine the batter
instructions.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a separate bowl. Mix half the dry ingredients into the butter mixture on low, followed by the milk, then the remaining dry ingredients. Fold in the entire date mixture, including its soaking liquid, just until uniform.

instructions.name: Bake the puddings
instructions.text: Divide the batter evenly among the ramekins, about a generous 1/2 cup each, and smooth the tops. Bake for 22 to 26 minutes, until risen and a tester has moist crumbs rather than wet batter; the centers should register 200°F to 205°F. Do not overbake.

instructions.name: Toast the pecans
instructions.text: While the puddings bake, spread the pecans in a small dry skillet and toast over medium-low heat for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring often, until fragrant and one shade darker. Transfer immediately to a board, cool and chop roughly.

instructions.name: Cook the toffee sauce
instructions.text: Combine the sauce butter, 3/4 cup brown sugar, cream, molasses and 1/4 teaspoon salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a gentle boil over medium heat, whisking until smooth, then reduce to medium-low and simmer for 4 minutes. Remove from the heat and stir in the remaining 1 teaspoon vanilla.

instructions.name: Soak and rest
instructions.text: Let the baked puddings cool for 5 minutes. Poke each six times with a skewer and spoon 1 tablespoon warm sauce over each. Rest for 10 minutes so the sauce soaks in while the crumb firms enough to unmold.

instructions.name: Unmold and finish
instructions.text: Run a thin knife around each ramekin and invert one pudding onto every plate. Remove the parchment, spoon over enough warm sauce to coat the top and cascade down the sides, and scatter with chopped pecans to match the photographed dessert. Serve the remaining sauce at the table.

why_it_works: Hot water and baking soda soften the dates and help them disperse through the batter, creating a moist crumb without dense pieces at the bottom.
Individual ramekins bake quickly and evenly, while a brief sauce soak adds flavor without collapsing the puddings before unmolding.
Dark brown sugar and a measured spoonful of molasses give the sauce deep caramel character; toasted pecans add the crisp contrast visible in every serving.
swaps: Use Deglet Noor dates if Medjool dates are unavailable, but weigh the same pitted amount and extend the hot-water soak to 20 minutes because they are firmer.
For a nut-free dessert, omit the pecans and finish with a pinch of flaky salt or 1/3 cup toasted pumpkin seeds if seeds are safe for your guests.
Bake the batter in one buttered 8-inch square metal pan for 28 to 34 minutes, checking for moist crumbs and a 200°F center before removing it.
storage: Cool puddings and sauce promptly and refrigerate them in separate airtight containers within 2 hours for up to 4 days. Reheat each pudding covered in a 300°F oven for 10 to 12 minutes, until 165°F, and warm the sauce gently in a saucepan without boiling. Freeze unsauced puddings for up to 2 months; thaw overnight in the refrigerator before reheating.
notes: Use oven-safe 6-ounce ramekins and leave at least 1/2 inch of headspace. Smaller cups may overflow and larger ones produce flatter puddings.
The sauce thickens as it cools. Rewarm it over low heat with 1 tablespoon cream if it no longer pours in a slow ribbon.
Toast pecans separately rather than simmering them in the sauce so they remain crisp against the soft pudding and glossy topping.

faqs.q: Can I make sticky toffee pudding before guests arrive?
faqs.a: Yes. Bake the puddings and make the sauce up to 2 days ahead, but store them separately. Reheat the puddings covered to 165°F, warm the sauce gently and assemble just before serving so the cakes stay tender rather than saturated.

faqs.q: Why did my puddings sink in the center?
faqs.a: They were likely underbaked, the batter was overmixed or the oven door opened early. Mix only until combined, keep the door closed for 20 minutes and confirm a 200°F to 205°F center before removing the ramekins. A slight settling is normal.

faqs.q: Do the dates make sticky toffee pudding taste fruity?
faqs.a: Not strongly. After soaking and mashing, dates provide moisture and a deep caramel-like sweetness more than a distinct fruit flavor. Small pieces remain in the crumb, but the brown-sugar toffee sauce is the dominant finish.
